heroHeadline: Taiwan Passes NT$780B (US$24.8B) Special Defense Budget — Largest in History; KMT-TPP 59-0 With 48 Abstentions; PLA 12 Sorties (10 Cross Median Line); 6 Days to Trump-Xi Summit; $14B PAC-3/NASAMS Still Pending
heroSubtitle: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed the NT$780 billion (US$24.8 billion) Special Law for Procuring Defense Equipment on May 8, 2026 — the largest defense budget in Taiwan's history — via KMT-TPP legislative majority (59-0, 48 abstentions), 6 days before the May 14-15 Trump-Xi Beijing summit. The bill is structured in two phases: Phase 1 (NT$300B) funds already-approved December 2025 US arms (82 HIMARS launchers, M109A7 howitzers, Javelin and TOW missiles); Phase 2 (NT$480B) is designated for an anticipated second US arms package. The $14 billion PAC-3 MSE / NASAMS package remains on hold — US officials confirmed it will not be announced until after Trump's Beijing visit. The NT$780B figure is a compromise: 37.5% below DPP's NT$1.25T request but endorsed by AIT, INDOPACOM, and US Congress as sufficient to demonstrate resolve. On the military front, PLA posted 12 sorties on May 8 with 10 crossing the median line into northern, southwestern, and eastern ADIZ sectors — sustained elevated pressure alongside 6 PLAN vessels and 2 official ships, de-escalating from the 22-sortie surge of May 7 but remaining well above baseline. The May pre-summit sortie sequence: 4 (May 1) → 29 record (May 2) → 1 (May 3) → 2 (May 4) → 1 (May 5) → 0 (May 6) → 22 (May 7) → 12 (May 8). Xi Jinping has confirmed Taiwan as the top priority for the summit, where Beijing is expected to press Trump to limit future arms sales and oppose Taiwan independence. Taiwan Deputy FM Francois Wu: 'What we are most afraid of is to put Taiwan on the menu of the talk between Xi Jinping and President Trump.'
